headline: A week-long parade of storms starts Monday night, bringing widespread rain, gusty winds and repeated coastal flooding, with the heaviest rain Wednesday night into Thanksgiving and rising tides along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines later in the week.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A slow-moving low-pressure system off the coast keeps sending light rain to the lowlands and snow showers to the mountains Sunday night, with most of the activity over the coast and the Olympics, so Sequim, Port Angeles and the Puget Sound lowlands should see only light rain at most. Snow levels sit around 2,000–3,000 feet, and a Winter Weather Advisory runs from 6 PM Sunday to 4 PM Monday for the Olympics, where Hurricane Ridge could pick up several inches of snow. Lows fall into the mid 30s to low 40s.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: The offshore low gets swept into the broader storm pattern Monday, and the first of several fronts spreads widespread rain across the region Monday night into Tuesday. Gusty southeast winds over 40 mph are nearly certain Monday and Tuesday, mainly along the coast and in San Juan and Island counties. Snow levels rise from 3,000–4,500 feet Monday evening to 4,000–5,500 feet Tuesday evening, so the higher passes such as Stevens get some snow but no major accumulation is expected. Rain turns to lingering showers Tuesday night, with near-normal temperatures through the period: highs close to 50 and lows in the 40s.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: More fronts keep coming Wednesday through Sunday, each bringing another round of widespread rain and breezy winds. Rain looks heaviest Wednesday night into Thursday (Thanksgiving), especially over the Olympics, and the Skokomish River is expected to reach flood stage around midweek and possibly moderate flood stage; a Hydrologic Outlook has been issued, though no widespread river flooding is expected. Weak high pressure may bring a brief break Friday, but the discussion says little about the weekend on land.

coast: A Coastal Flood Warning runs from 8 AM to 2 PM Monday for the Grays Harbor County coast, where moderate flooding is expected at Monday morning's high tide in places like Ocean Shores and Westport, and a Coastal Flood Advisory covers the same hours for the northern Washington coast and the eastern and western Strait of Juan de Fuca, with minor flooding possible as far east as Port Angeles. Confidence is growing that moderate to major coastal flooding could hit parts of the Grays Harbor County coast with Wednesday's high tides, made worse by high surf, and tides climb more significantly along the Strait and Puget Sound shorelines from Tuesday onward, which forecasters will monitor closely. On the water, a Gale Warning covers the east entrance of the Strait from 10 PM Sunday to 3 PM Tuesday; Small Craft Advisories cover the central and west Strait (10 PM Sunday to 4 AM Tuesday), Admiralty Inlet and the San Juans (10 PM Sunday to 10 PM Monday) and the Grays Harbor Bar (until 10 PM Monday), where rough conditions likely last most of the week. Offshore, a Storm Warning (outer waters, 10–60 miles out) and a Gale Warning (inner waters, within 10 miles) run from 7 AM Monday to 3 PM Tuesday, with a 60–75% chance of storm-force gusts in the outer waters by late Monday afternoon; seas of 10–13 feet keep building and stay steep and confused much of the week. Another round of strong gales and possibly storm-force gusts comes late Wednesday into Thursday, with gales likely (over 70%) over the coastal waters and eastern Strait into Thanksgiving and at least 23–29 mph (20–25 knot) winds on all waters; weak high pressure brings a brief letup in wind Friday, but seas stay high into the weekend.
watch_for: Coastal flooding: moderate flooding Monday morning on the Grays Harbor coast, possibly moderate to major Wednesday, and rising tides along the Strait and Puget Sound shorelines (including Port Angeles) later in the week.
Heavy rain Wednesday night into Thanksgiving and the Skokomish River reaching flood stage midweek.
Southeast wind gusts over 40 mph Monday and Tuesday along the coast and in the San Juan and Island counties.
confidence: Forecasters are very confident in the gusty winds Monday and Tuesday and in a stormy, wet pattern through the week, with growing confidence in Wednesday's coastal flooding on the Grays Harbor coast, while impacts along the Strait and Puget Sound shorelines later in the week are still uncertain.
